lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Application or project: handwashing a small item

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice handwashing a small item. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A trusted adult identifies one real small item with a visible stain, such as a bandana, a sports sock, or a cloth napkin.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult stays present for the entire pretreat-wash-rinse sequence.
Use only cool or lukewarm water; never water hot enough to be uncomfortable to the touch.
Check with the adult before using any stain-treatment product beyond plain detergent; some products require adult-only handling.

simulationAlternative.description: If no stained item is available, the learner instead studies a printed photo or description of a stained item and writes the four-step plan they would follow (identify the stain, pretreat, wash, rinse and check), including one reason pretreating before washing works better than washing first.

materials: learner-local: a place to hang the item to dry

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain why pretreating a stain before washing the whole item works better than washing the whole item first and hoping the stain comes out.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Pretreatment technique: Detergent is targeted at the stain and allowed to sit before washing. | Observation and next step: Result is described accurately (gone, lighter, unchanged) and a specific next step is named if needed. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner pretreat and wash a second stained item using a different pretreatment wait time (for example five minutes instead of two) and compare which wait time got a better result.

duration.sessionPattern: 5 minutes model, 5–7 minutes guided try, 10–15 minutes learner task, 5 minutes evidence and retry check
duration.adultTime: 10–20 minutes for permission, required supervision or review, and physical-event attestation

resources.title: handwashing a small item worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A trusted adult identifies one real small item with a visible stain, such as a bandana, a sports sock, or a cloth napkin.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact handwashing a small item decision or action.
Model move 2: Look closely at the stain with your adult before starting.
Model move 3: With your adult present, rub a small amount of detergent directly into the stained area and let it sit for two minutes before wetting the whole item.

Model check: Pretreatment technique: Detergent is targeted at the stain and allowed to sit before washing. | Observation and next step: Result is described accurately (gone, lighter, unchanged) and a specific next step is named if needed.

resources.title: handwashing a small item action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for handwashing a small item.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: handwashing a small item coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A trusted adult identifies one real small item with a visible stain, such as a bandana, a sports sock, or a cloth napkin.
Coach direction: Look closely at the stain with your adult before starting.
Learner prompt: Describe the stain: what color is it, roughly how large, and where on the item is it located?
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: handwashing a small item complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: With your adult present, rub a small amount of detergent directly into the stained area and let it sit for two minutes before wetting the whole item.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I rubbed detergent directly onto the stain, not just onto the whole item evenly.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I let the pretreated stain sit for about two minutes before wetting the item.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I then washed and rinsed the whole item using the four-step routine from third grade.

Equal-access rule: If no stained item is available, the learner instead studies a printed photo or description of a stained item and writes the four-step plan they would follow (identify the stain, pretreat, wash, rinse and check), including one reason pretreating before washing works better than washing first.

resources.title: handwashing a small item minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain why pretreating a stain before washing the whole item works better than washing the whole item first and hoping the stain comes out.

Success checks: Pretreatment technique: Detergent is targeted at the stain and allowed to sit before washing. | Observation and next step: Result is described accurately (gone, lighter, unchanged) and a specific next step is named if needed.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: handwashing a small item supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional handwashing a small item condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Pretreatment technique: Detergent is targeted at the stain and allowed to sit before washing. | Observation and next step: Result is described accurately (gone, lighter, unchanged) and a specific next step is named if needed..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.
